title: Bansh (Mongolian small boiled dumplings)
steps: Mix the flour, water and salt into a smooth dough, knead for 5 minutes and rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the meat, onion, garlic, salt, pepper and stock until the filling is sticky.
Roll out the dough thinly and cut into circles about 7 cm wide.
Put a small spoonful of filling in each and pinch closed into half-moons.
Boil in lightly salted water for 8 to 10 minutes until they float and the filling is cooked.
Serve with some of the cooking broth, or fry the boiled dumplings briefly for crisp edges.

title: Boortsog (Mongolian fried dough biscuits)
steps: Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl.
Stir in the melted butter, egg and enough milk to make a soft, pliable dough.
Knead briefly, cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Roll the dough out to about 1 cm thick and cut into diamonds, rectangles or knots.
Fry in oil heated to 160°C until golden brown all over, about 3 to 4 minutes.
Drain and serve with milk tea, dusting with sugar if you wish.

title: Khorkhog (Mongolian lamb and potatoes cooked with hot stones, stove-top version)

ingredients.name: bone-in lamb or mutton, in large pieces

steps: Rinse the meat and place it in a large heavy pot with the onion, garlic, salt, pepper and the water.
Bring to a boil, cover tightly and cook on low heat for 1 hour.
Add the carrots and potatoes, cover and cook another 30 minutes.
Add the cabbage on top and cook for 15 minutes more until everything is soft and the meat comes away from the bone.
Serve the meat and vegetables in a heap, with the broth in cups on the side.

title: Khuushuur (Mongolian fried meat pies)

ingredients.name: minced mutton or beef, with some fat

steps: Mix the flour, salt and warm water into a firm dough, knead briefly, cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the meat, onion, garlic, salt, pepper and cold water or stock by hand until the filling is sticky and juicy.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces and roll each into a thin circle about 15 cm wide.
Spread a thick layer of filling over half of each circle, fold over and press and crimp the edges firmly to seal.
Heat the oil to about 170°C and fry the pies for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden and the meat is cooked.
Drain on paper and serve hot.

title: Suutei tsai (Mongolian salted milk tea)
steps: Boil the water in a pot and add the tea, simmering for 5 minutes until dark and strong.
Pour in the milk and bring back to a gentle boil.
Ladle the tea up and pour it back from a height several times to cool and froth it.
Season with the salt and stir in the butter if using.
Strain into bowls and serve hot, optionally with a spoonful of toasted millet.

title: Tsuivan (Mongolian steamed noodles with meat and vegetables)
steps: Mix the flour, water and salt into a firm dough, knead well and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough out thin, cut into noodles about 5 mm wide, and spread them out to dry slightly.
Brown the meat in the oil, then add the onion, garlic and carrots and stir-fry for 5 minutes.
Lay the noodles on top of the meat and vegetables, add the soy sauce and a few tablespoons of water, cover and steam on low heat for 12 to 15 minutes.
Add the cabbage, cover, and cook 5 more minutes, then toss everything together and season to taste.

title: Ul boov (Mongolian Tsagaan Sar layered biscuit)

ingredients.measure: aaruul or dried curd and raisins
ingredients.name: to decorate

steps: Mix the flour, sugar and salt, then work in the melted fat and add warm water until you have a stiff dough.
Rest the dough for 30 minutes, then roll it out to about 1 cm thick.
Cut it into rectangles about 10 by 5 cm and press a pattern on top using a stamp or the back of a fork.
Bake at 180°C for 25 to 30 minutes until golden and firm.
Cool completely, then stack the biscuits in an odd number of layers and top with dried curds and raisins.
